Description: Repository scaffolding, CI, and dev environment for Ledger.
Build the gold question set and measurement harness before any retriever exists.
Pull SEC EDGAR filings and parse them into structured documents with routed elements.
Implement naive, structural, and contextual chunking plus table serialisation.
Embed chunks and index into OpenSearch for both dense (kNN) and lexical (BM25) retrieval.
Implement dense-only, BM25-only, hybrid RRF, and cross-encoder reranked retrieval.
Run all five configurations through the eval harness and record the before/after curve.
Generate cited answers and expose them via a bare Streamlit page.
README, DECISIONS.md, architecture diagram, and full-stack docker compose verification.
Videos and posts documenting the build for the portfolio.
Repository created with best-practice scaffolding: README with architecture diagram, MIT LICENSE, .gitignore, GitHub Actions CI (lint+test), issue/PR templates.

Summary: Set up Python project (pyproject.toml + src layout)
Description: src/ledger package layout with ingestion/chunking/indexing/retrieval/eval/serve subpackages; dev dependencies (ruff, mypy, pytest).

Summary: Docker compose skeleton for OpenSearch + app
Description: docker-compose.yml bringing up OpenSearch (single-node) and the app container; docker compose up must run the whole stack per Definition of Done.
Add .pre-commit-config.yaml and document install step in CONTRIBUTING.md.
Define the Q/A record schema: question, answer span, source document/page, difficulty band, filing reference(s).
Standalone retrieval-quality metrics independent of Ragas, computed per configuration.
Band 1 of the gold set. Example: 'What was total revenue for FY2024?'. Expected baseline recall ~0.95.
Band 2. Requires combining two tables, often on different pages, e.g. YoY segment operating margin change.
Band 3. Paragraph is materially wrong without its footnote — this is where naive chunking fails. E.g. restated figures.
Band 4. Requires retrieving and comparing across two filings, e.g. risk factor language change between Q2 and Q3.
Wire up Ragas for context recall, context precision, and faithfulness scoring against the gold set.
`make eval` writes/updates the before/after table in RESULTS.md automatically.
Fetch 10-K/10-Q filings via the EDGAR full-text search / submissions API, respecting rate limits and required User-Agent header.
Parse fetched filings with Docling into a structured document representation (sections, tables, footnotes).
Route parsed elements to the correct downstream path: prose to chunkers, tables to the serialiser.
Serialise multi-page tables to markdown with an attached caption, preserved as a unit rather than split by token count.
Fixed-size token chunking baseline, no structure awareness.
Chunk boundaries respect document section structure (not just token count).
Each chunk is prefixed with an LLM-generated summary of its surrounding context before embedding.

Summary: Wire table serialiser output into structural/contextual chunkers
Description: Ensure serialised tables flow into the structural and contextual chunking paths per architecture diagram.
Batch-embed all chunk variants with bge-large.
Create and populate the OpenSearch kNN index from embedded chunks.
Create and populate the OpenSearch BM25 lexical index from raw chunk text.
Baseline retrieval using only the kNN vector index.
Baseline retrieval using only the lexical index.

Summary: Hybrid retriever with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Description: Combine dense and BM25 results via RRF in a single OpenSearch-backed pipeline.
Rerank hybrid RRF results with a cross-encoder; measure recall gain vs added p95 latency.
First eval run through the harness; establishes the baseline row of the results table. Milestone per build sequence.
Run structural+dense, structural+hybrid RRF, contextual+hybrid RRF, and +rerank through the eval harness.
Capture p95 latency per configuration alongside recall/MRR/faithfulness.
Fill in ADR-003 and ADR-004 (contextual chunking cost/benefit, rerank latency tradeoff) with actual measured numbers.

Summary: LLM answer generation with citation enforcement
Description: Generate answers strictly grounded in retrieved source spans; a wrong-but-confident answer is treated as a bug.
Bare Streamlit page showing the answer alongside the cited source spans.

Summary: Finalize README above-the-fold diagram and results
Description: README leads with the Mermaid architecture diagram and the results curve, not a demo screenshot.

Summary: Complete DECISIONS.md for all five ADRs
Description: OpenSearch vs Qdrant, hand-built evals vs synthetic, contextual chunking cost/benefit, rerank latency tradeoff, table serialisation approach — all resolved with rationale.
Confirm `docker compose up` brings up OpenSearch and the app end-to-end from a clean checkout.
Walk the checklist in the project spec end-to-end before calling the project shipped.
